content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a specialized application of the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10), to address deaths occurring during the perinatal period. This system, known as ICD-PM (ICD-Perinatal Mortality), is designed to improve the classification and reporting of perinatal deaths, which include stillbirths and neonatal deaths occurring within the first seven days of life. The ICD-PM is modeled after the WHO’s application of ICD-10 for maternal mortality (ICD-MM) and adheres to the coding rules established in ICD-10. The ICD-PM system is intended to facilitate the consistent collection, analysis, and interpretation of data related to perinatal deaths. It aims to improve the accuracy of death attribution by identifying underlying causes and linking them to maternal conditions when applicable. This approach is particularly important in regions with high perinatal mortality rates, where deaths are often underreported or poorly documented. The ICD-PM system has three key features: 1. Timing of Death: It captures the timing of perinatal deaths in relation to their occurrence, categorizing them as antepartum (before the onset of labor), intrapartum (during labor but before delivery), or neonatal (up to the seventh day of postnatal life). While primarily designed for early neonatal deaths, the system can also be applied to late neonatal deaths if they are a consequence of events during the perinatal period. 2. Multilayered Classification: The system employs a multilayered approach to classify causes of death, reflecting varying levels of available information depending on the setting. This ensures that even in resource-limited environments, meaningful data can be captured and analyzed. 3. Maternal Condition Linkage: The ICD-PM links contributing maternal conditions to perinatal deaths, recognizing the close relationship between maternal health and perinatal outcomes. This linkage is required for every perinatal death, even if no maternal condition is identified, to ensure comprehensive documentation of the interconnected health outcomes of mothers and their babies. The ICD-PM system was developed by the WHO Working Group on Perinatal Death Classification and underwent pilot testing in databases from the United Kingdom and South Africa. It is designed to be used by healthcare providers, death certifiers, program managers, statistical offices, and researchers to improve the accuracy and consistency of perinatal death reporting. The document outlining the ICD-PM system includes guidance on its development, a grouping system for identifying perinatal deaths using existing ICD-10 codes, and instructions for linking maternal conditions to perinatal outcomes. It also provides annexes and tables to facilitate the consistent reporting of clinical conditions, identification of codes for perinatal deaths based on timing, and documentation of maternal conditions contributing to perinatal outcomes. By standardizing the attribution of causes of death, the ICD-PM system aims to enhance the interpretation of perinatal mortality data, improve resource allocation for maternal and neonatal health programs, and ultimately reduce preventable perinatal deaths. The system aligns with the recommendations of the Every Newborn Action Plan, which emphasizes the importance of capturing maternal complications as part of perinatal death registration. The WHO encourages countries to adopt the ICD-PM system and recommends its use in conjunction with the three volumes of ICD-10. This approach will improve the usability and comparability of perinatal mortality statistics, reduce errors in coding, and support targeted interventions to address the underlying causes of perinatal deaths.
